 ABC News News Home Flood warnings as Queensland braces for more wild weather Share Share article Flood warnings as Queensland braces for more wild weather
 By Josh Dye
 Topic: Floods
 Posted Sun 25 Oct 2026 at 10:27am Sun 25 Oct 2026 at 10:27am Sun 25 Oct 2026 at 10:27am , updated Sun 25 Oct 2026 at 11:33am Sun 25 Oct 2026 at 11:33am Sun 25 Oct 2026 at 11:33am Netherby Road at Gundiah on the Fraser Coast under water after heavy rain. ( Supplied: Fraser Coast Regional Council ) 
 abc.net.au/news/flood-warnings-queensland-braces-for-more-rain-storms/107306066 Link copied Share Share article Several flood warnings have been issued across Queensland, as the state endures another day of heavy rain and residents brace for severe storms still to come. 
 A Watch and Act alert has been issued for people in the Central Highlands as the river rises around the Theresa Creek Dam catchment area.
 Residents in Clermont and surrounding areas are being told to prepare now due to flooding, although the situation has been downgraded from an Emergency Warning earlier in the day.
 In the state's south-east, the Mary River at Tiaro, north of Gympie, is rising and could reach the major flood level.
 Flood gauges show the Mary River is rising rapidly above the moderate level, following days of heavy downpours. 
 A flooded bridge over Sandy Creek just outside Clermont. ( Supplied: Jess Keyte ) 
 In the past week, parts of the Mary River catchment have had more than 300 millimetres of rain, while some areas of the Sunshine Coast have had upwards of 400mm. 
 The Bureau of Meteorology warns a severe weather system over the state's inland area will move east today, shifting to the south-east by Monday and bringing more heavy rain.
 "There's still multiple days of storms and potentially severe storms to come, with Monday probably the peak day in terms of south-east Queensland risk," senior forecaster Felim Hanniffy said. 
 "And it will be the trifecta – that's large hail, damaging winds and heavy rainfall."
 There are also moderate flood warnings in place for the Warrego River and the Weir River.
